Notes: THE FEEL OF THE WHOLE GAME LIVES IN THIS FILE. A button that does nothing when the mouse is over it reads as a picture of a button. Two pixels up and three per cent bigger, over a tenth of a second, is enough to read as 'this is a thing you can press' and little enough that a row of eight of them is not a disco. Ease `out` means it moves fast and settles - which is how a real object behaves and a linear move does not.

AND DOWN AGAIN. Shorter than the hover and in the opposite direction, so a press feels like a press. Ease `in` is the right way round here: a press starts slow and arrives, because your finger is what is doing the work.
Back to rest. Longer than the press, so it springs rather than snaps.

A WINDOW OVER THE BASE. It comes up from slightly below at ninety-four per cent and settles - which reads as a thing arriving rather than a thing appearing. Scale under 1 means it grows INTO place; over 1 would mean it shrinks into place, which reads as a thing being put away.
Faster than opening. Closing a window is never the interesting part.
A whole screen arriving. It is a fade: Move and Scale are both nothing, and only Seconds matters.
And leaving. Shorter than arriving, always - waiting to leave is the most annoying wait there is.
HOW FAST A LINE OF DIALOGUE TYPES ITSELF, in seconds per character. 0 shows the whole line at once. 0.02 is a comfortable read-along; 0.05 is slow enough to be annoying on a long line.
A player card arriving in the draft row. From below and small, so a row of them deals like a hand of cards.
And the one you chose, lifting out of the row.
THE REFEREE COMING ON. Move X is negative because he comes from off the LEFT edge. See ref_window.gd - a referee who appears instantly reads as a bug and a referee who walks on reads as a referee.

A GOAL. The one moment in the game that is allowed to be loud: the screen swells eight per cent and shakes seven pixels. Shake is in pixels and it is multiplied by `juice_scale` in Tuning.csv, so a player who dislikes screen shake can turn this off without you editing it.
A yellow or a red. Smaller than a goal, because a booking is a bad moment and bad moments should not feel like fireworks.
